findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:119: align-items() omits -moz-box-align even though flexbox() emits display: -moz-box, causing Firefox versions using that fallback to retain stretch alignment instead of vertically centering header and small-action contents. Add -moz-box-align: $alignment.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:119: align-items() omits -moz-box-align even though flexbox() emits display: -moz-box, causing Firefox versions using that fallback to retain stretch alignment instead of vertically centering header and small-action contents. Add -moz-box-align: $alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that flexbox() mixin includes 'display: -moz-box' for Firefox fallback, but the align-items() mixin at line 119 does not include '-moz-box-align: $alignment'. This is a real inconsistency - if the code uses -moz-box display, it should also use -moz-box-align for alignment to work properly in older Firefox versions. The finding correctly identifies that this omission would cause alignment issues in Firefox versions that use the -moz-box fallback.
